newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans warn summit may isolate Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans warn summit may isolate Israel.

text.p: Republican leaders of the U.S. Congress on Sunday warned President Bill Clinton that this week's upcoming summit between Israeli and Palestinian leaders could serve to isolate Israel.

"We believe it would be counterproductive to the long-term prospects for peace in the Middle East if next week's meeting is used as an opportunity to pressure Israel to make unilateral concessions in the face of violence aimed at its people," House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Senate Majority Trent Lott wrote in a letter to Clinton.

Clinton announced on Sunday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would come to Washington for high-level meetings this week, tentatively slated for Tuesday and Wednesday.

Gingrich and Lott said they shared Clinton's desire to stop the violence. "Nonetheless, we are deeply concerned were deeply concerned that the meeting... may serve to isolate Israel and strengthen the position of those Palestinians who believe that violence serves their purposes," they wrote.

They warned that any move to isolate Israel "would not only threaten the security of our most faithful ally in that region; it would also frustrate the pursuit of a secure and lasting peace in the Middle East."

They also urged that the summit address the roles of Iran, Syria, the Palestinian Islamic movement Hamas, and the Lebanese Hizbollah militia in "destabilizing the region", saying the United States should take the lead in forging a global strategy to combat state-sponsored terrorism.
